text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- State oil company NNPC says it expects two fuel-laden vessels on Monday to ease petrol shortages in commercial capital Lagos.
- Nigeria's airspace remains among safest in world despite a spate of accidents in recent months, Fidelis Kaigama, director-general at the aviation ministry, says.
- Traders sell a bag of cement above the 300 naira ceiling price fixed by the military government in January, paper says, quoting own investigation.
- Striker Daniel Amokachi's brace of goals gives Nigeria a 2-1 win over Guinea in a World Cup qualifier and puts the Olympic champions top of their group.

- Government's reduction of crude allocation for local consumption to 250,000 bpd from 320,000 bpd since January has created technical problems for Nigeria's four refineries and is responsible for a persistent fuel crisis in the country, NNPC sources say.

- The 7th Organisation of African Unity (OAU) trade and tourism fair, staged in northern city of Kaduna, ends on Sunday; organisers say they are impressed with the attendance from 18 African countries at the nine-day fair.

- Nigerian navy says it has seized 12 boats containing weapons owned by Ijaw tribesmen who two weeks ago held hostage 127 staff of Royal/Dutch Shell at oil stations in the swamps to protest against the relocation of a municipal council headquarters.
